navy:
UNITED STATES (faction key `nato`) — SURFACE FLEET ONLY. 26 surface hulls across six eras (35 naval defs minus 9 sub-layer boats owned by the other workflows). Roles present: patrol, corvette (= DE/FF/FFG/LCS), destroyer, cruiser, carrier, missileboat. No amphibious warfare ship, no minelayer/minesweeper, no Iowa, no Zumwalt, no Essex/Baltimore, no Leahy/Belknap/Virginia CGN, no Kidd — the shared `both`-faction lst / navminelayer / minesweeper / oiler / repair_sea hulls are the only amphib/MCM/logistics afloat and they are common to all eight factions.

Everything below was RESOLVED under jsc from a concatenation of stub + util.js + config.js + facts.js + rules.js + eras.js + heavyair.js + generations.js, i.e. after generations.js rewrites. Measured, not read off the source line. A separate grep confirmed no file loaded after generations.js writes `.weapons`, `WEAPONS[...]` or `Object.assign(UNITS...)`, so that resolution is final.

Two measured facts frame the whole audit:
(1) `nato`'s DOMAIN row in generations.js is `naval:1.00` and every other multiplier 1.00, so — uniquely among the eight factions — no American unit ever gets a privateWeapon() clone from the domain pass. The source line in eras.js IS the final answer for this faction, and only this faction.
(2) Every generated naval weapon id `w_<era>_nato_<role>` is CARRIED BY 2-4 NATIONS. w_e90_nato_destroyer is on the Arleigh Burke, the Type 42 Batch 3, the Cassard and the Brandenburg. So no American ship can be corrected by editing its own weapon without renaming European ones.

=== AREA AIR DEFENCE, measured against the actual mechanic ===
combat.js areaSam() (line 212-248) counts a unit as an area air-defence host only if it carries a weapon with `tgt.air` AND `proj === "missile"`. Of the 26 US surface hulls, exactly TWO pass: cruiser_n and destroyer_n, both e20-roster. Zero in e50, e60, e80, e90, e00.
Cross-checked across all 8 factions and all 6 eras: of 176 sea-layer hulls in the game, the only era-roster ships that pass are pact_e60/e90/e00_carrier — and they pass by accident, because the Moskva's weapon "14 x Ka-25 ASW helicopters" was authored as proj:"missile", tgt:{air}. There is no era-roster ship in the game, of any navy, that was deliberately given fleet air defence.

=== LAND ATTACK, measured ===
Every hull has SOME ground:1 weapon because every naval gun carries ground:1 — naval gunfire is modelled and modelled everywhere. The land-attack MISSILE picture is: the only ground-capable guided rounds on a US surface ship are ssm_harpoon (r14), ssm_nsm (r16) and w_e80_nato_missileboat (r12.7). `tlam_n` "BGM-109 Tomahawk" (r19, d320) EXISTS in the weapon table and is carried by exactly one American hull in the whole game: ssgn_n, the converted Ohio. No Burke, no Ticonderoga, no Spruance, in any era.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: each carries exactly one weapon, a gun with tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1}. nato_e80_cruiser (USS Ticonderoga CG-47, service 1983) = 'Two 127mm/54 Mk 45'. nato_e90_destroyer (USS Arleigh Burke DDG-51, service 1991) = a weapon LITERALLY NAMED '90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha' whose proj is 'shell' at 720 m/s and whose tgt mask has air:0. combat.js areaSam() requires tgt.air && proj==='missile'; not one of these four qualifies. An Aegis cruiser in this game cannot fire at an aircraft at all.
findings.whatIsReal: CG-47 commissioned 22 Jan 1983 with SPY-1A and two Mk 26 twin launchers holding 68 SM-2MR — the first ship in the world able to track hundreds of contacts and guide many missiles at once. CG-52 Bunker Hill (1986) replaced the arms with 122 Mk 41 cells. DDG-51 commissioned 4 July 1991 with SPY-1D and 90 Mk 41 cells. Fleet area air defence from 1983 is the single most important capability line in this navy and the game draws none of it before the e20 roster.
findings.fix: Append a real area SAM to each hull. The mechanism already exists and works — cruiser_n/destroyer_n use sam_sm2 and register correctly. Edits E7, E9, E10, E11 below add sam_sm2mr (a new e80/e90-honest RIM-66 SM-2MR) and sam_sm2 (e00), plus the Harpoon, ASROC-class torpedo and Phalanx each hull actually carried.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: one weapon, id w_e60_nato_cruiser, NAME 'Terrier and Talos SAM launchers', proj 'shell', speed 720, range 9.4, tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1}. A weapon whose own name is two surface-to-air missile systems, which cannot engage air. The unit desc adds 'the first all-missile cruiser - built with no guns at all until Kennedy reportedly objected'.
findings.whatIsReal: CGN-9 commissioned 9 Sep 1961 with two Mk 10 twin Terrier launchers forward and one Mk 12 Talos aft, and NO guns whatsoever until two 5in/38 were added in 1962-63. Its entire reason for existing was long-range fleet air defence. This is the exact defect class found on the Los Angeles/Seawolf/Virginia: the prose names a capability the weapon list does not deliver.
findings.fix: Edit E3: append the new rules.js weapon sam_terrier ('RIM-2 Terrier / RIM-8 Talos', r10.2, proj missile, tgt air) to the unit. The gun row is left alone because w_e60_nato_cruiser is also carried by gbr_e60_cruiser (Tiger CL) and fra_e60_cruiser (Colbert) — renaming it there is a separate, wider fix.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: no American surface warship in any of the six eras carries tlam_n. cruiser_n = navgun_mk45, sam_sm2, ssm_harpoon, asw_mk54, ciws_phalanx. destroyer_n = the identical five. Meanwhile js/facts.js line 20 states cruiser_n's armament as '122-cell Mk 41 VLS (SM-2, Tomahawk, VLA)...' and line 23 states destroyer_n's as '96-cell Mk 41 VLS (SM-2/SM-6/ESSM/Tomahawk/VLA)'. The weapon tlam_n 'BGM-109 Tomahawk' (r19, d320, tgt {ground,sea}) is defined and works — it is carried by exactly one unit in the game, ssgn_n.
findings.whatIsReal: The first Tomahawk fired from a US surface ship was from USS Merrill (DD-976) in 1983 using armoured box launchers; ABLs went onto eight Spruances and onto the reactivated Iowas from 1983-84. The first Mk 41 VLS Tomahawk ship was USS Bunker Hill (CG-52) in 1986. On 17 Jan 1991 Bunker Hill, San Jacinto and Paul F. Foster opened Desert Storm with them. Since then TLAM from a Mk 41 farm has been the most-fired American weapon there is, and it is the thing a Burke or a Ticonderoga is FOR against a land target. The game's own facts table promises it and the loadout does not have it.
findings.fix: Edits E6, E9, E10, E11, E14 add tlam_n to nato_e80_destroyer (Spruance, ABL from 1983), nato_e90_cruiser, nato_e90_destroyer, nato_e00_destroyer, and to cruiser_n/destroyer_n in the rules.js NAVY table. Deliberately NOT added to nato_e80_cruiser: CG-47 to CG-51 had Mk 26 arm launchers that could not fire Tomahawk, and CG-47 is the hull the unit names.

findings.whatIsReal: DDG-2 commissioned 10 Sep 1960 with a Mk 11 twin Tartar launcher aft, two 5in/54 Mk 42 and ASROC. RIM-24 Tartar reached the fleet on this class. The ship exists because of a SAM the game does not give it.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: one weapon 'Two 127mm/54 Mk 45', tgt {ground,sea}. Its own desc: 'the empty space then absorbed vertical launch cells and Tomahawk, making it the most heavily armed destroyer afloat by the end of the decade.' No VLS field, no Tomahawk, no air defence of any kind, no ASW weapon on the class built to do ASW.
findings.whatIsReal: DD-963 commissioned 20 Sep 1975, deliberately under-armed with growth margin. Sea Sparrow BPDMS from commissioning, Phalanx from 1980, Harpoon from 1981, ABL Tomahawk from 1983 on eight hulls, 61-cell Mk 41 on twenty-four hulls from 1986, ASROC and Mk 32 tubes throughout, two SH-60B from 1984. By 1989 it was exactly what its own card says it was.
findings.fix: Edit E6: append sam_seasparrow (new, point defence — explicitly NOT an area system), ssm_harpoon, asw_mk54, tlam_n, ciws_phalanx.

findings.unit: nato_e80_corvette and nato_e90_corvette (Oliver Hazard Perry FFG-7)
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: nato_e80_corvette carries ONE weapon, named 'Mk 13 launcher for SM-1MR and Harpoon', proj 'shell', r7.3, tgt {ground,air,sea} — a launcher modelled as a gun, so no SM-1, no Harpoon, no area air defence. nato_e90_corvette is worse: its single weapon is a plain gun 'OTO 76mm Super Rapid' with no missile at all, so the SAME HULL LOSES its air-defence weapon between the 1980s and the 1990s. Its desc explains that the Mk 13 was removed — but in 2003, which is the e00 period, not e90.
findings.whatIsReal: FFG-7 commissioned 17 Dec 1977 with a Mk 13 single-arm launcher, a 40-round magazine of SM-1MR and Harpoon, one 76mm Mk 75 OTO Melara Compact (NOT the Super Rapid), one Phalanx, and two LAMPS helicopters. The Mk 13 came out class-wide in 2003-2004. Through the whole of the 1980s and 1990s the Perry is the US Navy's numerous escort and it has a missile.
findings.fix: Edits E5 and E8: append sam_sm1, ssm_harpoon, ciws_phalanx to both. The e90 hull keeps them because the Mk 13 removal belongs to e00, exactly as its own desc dates it.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: navgun_76 'OTO 76mm Super Rapid' + ciws_phalanx. Its own desc says 'a 57mm rapid-fire mount'. js/warship_specs.js line 172 draws it with gunCal:57. And the e00 version of the same ship, nato_e00_corvette, correctly carries a weapon named 'One 57mm Mk 110'. Three places in the codebase say 57mm and the loadout says 76mm Italian.
findings.whatIsReal: Both LCS variants mount the BAE Mk 110 57mm. Neither has a Phalanx gun: Freedom-class carries a 21-cell Mk 49 RAM launcher, Independence-class an 11-cell SeaRAM. This is precisely the complaint generations.js makes in its own NAVGUN comment — 'every navy was firing the same Italian gun' — and the NAVGUN table has no nato row, so the American case it was written about went unfixed.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED, a clean transposition. warship_specs.js line 158: nato_e00_carrier — the unit whose full name is 'USS Ronald Reagan (CVN-76), Nimitz class' and whose desc says in so many words 'The Gerald R. Ford does not exist yet in this period - she was not commissioned until 2017' — is given designation:'CVN-78 Gerald R. Ford class', len:317, beam:78. findings.fix: Edit E15/E16: swap the two designations and put the right hull dimensions with each.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: missileboat_n, fac nato, from e20, cost 1500, carrying ssm_harpoon and ciws_phalanx, buildable in the present-day roster. warship_specs.js line 176 gives it designation:'PHM-1 Pegasus'. Meanwhile eras.js line 9414 contains nato_e90_missileboat named '(none)', full 'No US Navy missile craft after 1993', desc 'the US Navy chose deliberately never to operate missile boats again' — and rules.js purgePhantomUnits() correctly deletes it. And nato_e80_missileboat's own desc calls Pegasus 'the honest historical basis for the game's Harpoon Missile Boat'.
findings.whatIsReal: The six Pegasus-class hydrofoils decommissioned on 30 July 1993 and the US Navy has operated no missile boat since. unitFor('nato','missileboat') returns NONE for e00 — correct — and then missileboat_n for e20, which is the one era where it is most certainly wrong. The data records the gap in three places and the roster sells the capability anyway.
findings.fix: NO EDIT PROPOSED — this is an owner's call, and the obvious route is a trap. Renaming missileboat_n to '(none)' triggers purgePhantomUnits()'s fallback, which would find nato_e80_missileboat (from e80) and extend its `to` to e20, putting a 1977 hydrofoil in 2020. The clean fix is to delete the missileboat_n entry from rules.js outright, which leaves the US with Pegasus in e80-e90 and nothing after — exactly what the e90 placeholder says. It touches SHIP_RCS, SOFTKILL, FIXED_MAGAZINE, NAVY, warship_specs.js, units3d_final.js and spriteart.js, so it deserves its own pass.

findings.unit: every w_<era>_nato_<role> naval weapon (the IFV defect, at sea)
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED by scanning eras.js for each id: w_e50_nato_carrier/corvette/cruiser are on 3 nations each, w_e50_nato_destroyer on 4, w_e60_nato_corvette on 4, w_e60_nato_cruiser on 3, w_e60_nato_destroyer on 4, w_e80_nato_destroyer on 4, w_e90_nato_corvette on 3, w_e90_nato_destroyer on 4, w_e00_nato_corvette on 4, w_e00_nato_destroyer on 4. Only w_e90_nato_cruiser is American-exclusive. Because the DOMAIN pass clones per-unit but COPIES THE NAME, HMS Tiger's main battery is displayed as 'Terrier and Talos SAM launchers'; HMS Manchester (Type 42 Batch 3), the Cassard and the Brandenburg all display '90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha'; the Daring, the Surcouf and the Fletcher-derived Z-1 all display 'Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts'; HMS Swiftsure and De Grasse both display 'Nine 203mm/55 Mk 16 rapid-fire guns'.
findings.whatIsReal: Tiger-class: two twin QF 6in Mk N5 and 3in/70. Type 42: one 4.5in Mk 8 and Sea Dart. Cassard: 100mm Mod 68 and SM-1MR. Brandenburg: 76mm OTO, Sea Sparrow VLS and two RAM mounts. This is the same defect as 'every IFV carried one 1983 American missile regardless of nation', reproduced across four navies at sea.
findings.fix: Structural, and outside this workflow's remit to change (it would rewrite British, French and German ships). RECORDED SO THE OWNER KNOWS. The consequence for THIS audit is a hard constraint that shaped every edit below: no American correction may touch a w_<era>_nato_<role> weapon's fields. Every edit is either an append to the American unit's own weapons array or a new American-only weapon in rules.js.

findings.unit: nato_e50_cruiser (Des Moines CA-134), nato_e50_destroyer (Forrest Sherman DD-931)
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: both carry a single weapon with tgt {ground:1, air:0, sea:1}. Neither can engage an aircraft. Note the internal contradiction: the SAME GUN, the 127mm/54 Mk 42, carries air:1 on nato_e60_corvette ('One 127mm/54 Mk 42') and air:0 on nato_e50_destroyer ('Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts'). Both cannot be right.
findings.whatIsReal: The Mk 42 is a dual-purpose mount — that is why the Navy bought it. Forrest Sherman commissioned 9 Nov 1955 with three of them plus four 3in/50. Des Moines commissioned 16 Nov 1948 with nine 8in/55 in the only fully automatic 8in turrets ever built, TWELVE 5in/38 in twin mounts and a heavy 3in/50 battery — an enormous anti-aircraft fit that is the whole reason a 1948 gun cruiser was still worth manning.
findings.fix: Edits E1 and E2. Des Moines gets aa_5in38 appended (the secondary battery, which is what engaged aircraft; the 8in main battery stays as the shared era weapon). Forrest Sherman's array is SWAPPED to a new American-only navgun_mk42 whose figures deliberately match w_e50_nato_destroyer exactly, so only the label and the air bit change — and it stops the American hull sharing a weapon with a Daring, a Surcouf and a Fletcher.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: rcs 0.1. Every other American era corvette is 0.6 — including nato_e80_corvette, which is the IDENTICAL Perry-class hull. 0.1 is the lowest surface radar cross-section in the game bar corvette_n, lower than the Tuo Chiang stealth catamaran (0.12), the La Fayette-derived corvette_f (0.18) and the Type 45 (0.30).
findings.whatIsReal: A 1977 Oliver Hazard Perry is a boxy, single-screw, flat-sided 1970s frigate with no signature shaping of any kind. rules.js's own SHIP_RCS comment is explicit that the number is driven by superstructure shaping; 0.1 is a copy of corvette_n's value that landed on the wrong row. SHIP_RCS drives both detection range (fourth root) and how easily an incoming missile holds lock, so this is not cosmetic.
findings.fix: Edit E12: 0.1 -> 0.6, matching the identical e80 hull.

findings.unit: all 20 era-roster warships of all eight factions
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED across the whole roster: zero era-roster naval units have a `helo` field and zero have `vls`. Twelve e20-roster ships have helo, six have vls. game.js:394 and entities.js:357 embark a helicopter complement only when def.helo or def.carrier is set; combat.js:352 gives a SAM host up to +50% effectiveness scaled by def.vls/220. So no warship of any navy before the present-day roster embarks a helicopter or gets magazine depth.
findings.whatIsReal: For the American fleet specifically: LAMPS I (SH-2 Seasprite) from 1971 on the Knox and Perry; LAMPS III (SH-60B) from 1984 on the Perry, Spruance and Ticonderoga; two SH-60B on every Ticonderoga from CG-47. rules.js's own NAVY comment calls the embarked helicopter 'the single biggest ASW multiplier'. Mk 41 VLS depth: 61 cells on 24 Spruances from 1986, 122 on CG-52 onward, 90 on DDG-51.
findings.fix: NO EDIT PROPOSED here — it is a whole-fleet, eight-faction change and giving it only to the Americans would be the symmetry error in reverse. Recorded with the American dates so a later pass has them.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: every American era corvette/frigate has NO `radar` field at all (19 era naval hulls across the game lack it, 17 have it — every American one lacks it). combat.js:263 closeInGuns() returns immediately on !e.def.radar, so a Perry's or a Knox's dual-purpose gun contributes nothing to air defence even though its tgt mask says air:1; and game.js:1112 skips it for radar reveal.
findings.whatIsReal: FFG-7 carries SPS-49, a capable long-range 2D air-search set, and an Mk 92 fire-control system; FF-1052 carries SPS-40. These ships aim their guns with radar.
findings.fix: NO EDIT PROPOSED — the pattern is roster-wide and the right value per hull is a judgement the owner should make. Flagged because it silently voids the air:1 bit these ships already carry.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: unitFor('nato','cruiser','e00') returns NONE. There is no nato_e00_cruiser row anywhere in eras.js. nato_e90_cruiser has to:'e90' and cruiser_n has from:'e20', so the 2000s have a hole. pact_e00_cruiser (Slava) exists, so this is not a roster-wide 'no cruisers in e00' design rule.
findings.whatIsReal: Twenty-two Ticonderogas were in commission throughout 2000-2009; the first five (Mk 26 arms) decommissioned 2004-2005 and the rest served well past 2010. The 2000s are a period when the US cruiser force was at its largest and most capable.
findings.fix: Either add a nato_e00_cruiser row (CG-52 class, service 1986, Mk 41 + SM-2 + TLAM) or set nato_e90_cruiser to:'e00'. The latter is a one-token change and matches what the hull actually did.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: desc reads 'Naval gunfire support that flattens a coastal base from 17 tiles out.' Its longest gun is navgun_mk45 at range 11.5. The number 17 is the range of navgun_203 '203mm main battery' — a weapon cruiser_n used to carry before the NAVY refit table replaced its loadout, and which is now carried by nothing at all.
findings.whatIsReal: An Mk 45 5in/54 firing conventional ammunition reaches about 24 km. The card promises a reach the ship does not have and quotes a number from a deleted weapon.
findings.fix: Reword to the real figure, or state the reach the weapon actually has. Trivial, but it is the same class of defect as the Tomahawk prose.

findings.unit: WEAPONS: navgun_203, navgun_127, ssm, sam_ship, depthchg; UNITS: shoreBombard
findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: those five weapons are referenced by no unit, no building and no privateWeapon clone — they are the original pre-NAVY-refit loadouts of cruiser_n, destroyer_n and missileboat_n, left behind when rules.js line 2814 Object.assign'd the NAVY table over them. Separately, `shoreBombard:true` is set on cruiser_n, cruiser_p and one other hull and is read by no code anywhere in js/.
findings.whatIsReal: n/a — housekeeping. Worth knowing because navgun_203's range is the source of the false '17 tiles' claim above, and because a reader of rules.js line 626 reasonably assumes shoreBombard does something.
findings.fix: Delete the five orphans, or leave them and note they are unreferenced. Decide whether shoreBombard should gate the bombard order or be removed.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: descs are hard-truncated at exactly 320 characters. Of the 22 American naval descs, 15 end mid-sentence or mid-word: nato_e80_cruiser ends '...Note for the game - a ', nato_e00_destroyer ends '...Naval Strike Missile and Mar', nato_e50_carrier ends '...SCB-125 to take the angl', nato_e60_cruiser ends '...points directly at Aeg'.
findings.whatIsReal: n/a — a generation artefact, not a history error. Global to eras.js and to all eight factions.
findings.fix: Out of scope for this workflow; recorded with the exact cut length so whoever regenerates eras.js can raise or remove the cap.

findings.whatTheGameHas: CHECKED every from:/to:/service: field against real commissioning. Des Moines 1948, Dealey 1954, Forrestal 1955, Forrest Sherman 1955, Adams 1960, Enterprise 1961, Long Beach 1961, Knox 1969, Spruance 1975, Nimitz 1975, Perry 1977, Pegasus 1977, Ticonderoga 1983, Arleigh Burke 1991, Flight IIA 2000, Reagan 2003, LCS 2008, Ford 2017 (stated in the desc).
findings.whatIsReal: Every one matches: CA-134 16 Nov 1948; DE-1006 3 Jun 1954; CVA-59 1 Oct 1955; DD-931 9 Nov 1955; DDG-2 10 Sep 1960; CVN-65 25 Nov 1961; CGN-9 9 Sep 1961; FF-1052 12 Apr 1969; DD-963 20 Sep 1975; CVN-68 3 May 1975; FFG-7 17 Dec 1977; PHM-1 9 Jul 1977; CG-47 22 Jan 1983; DDG-51 4 Jul 1991; DDG-79 19 Aug 2000; CVN-76 12 Jul 2003; LCS-1 8 Nov 2008; CVN-78 22 Jul 2017.
findings.fix: None. The dates are sound throughout, including the units that carry no explicit service field. This was checked specifically because an earlier audit is said to have missed units without a service field.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: eras.js authors nato_e80_missileboat with to:'e80', and a separate nato_e90_missileboat named '(none)', full 'No US Navy missile craft after 1993'. rules.js isPhantomUnit()/purgePhantomUnits() deletes the placeholder so it cannot be bought, then finds the earlier hull in the same role and extends its `to` to e90. Resolved result: Pegasus available e80-e90, nothing after.
findings.whatIsReal: PHM-1 commissioned 9 July 1977, PHM-2 to PHM-6 in 1981-82, all six decommissioned 30 July 1993 — squarely inside the e90 window. The machinery produced exactly the right answer, and the placeholder row is a model of the realism-over-symmetry rule stated plainly in the data.
findings.fix: None. Recorded because it is the pattern the missileboat_n finding above should be fixed to match, and because the same mechanism is the reason boat_n and the '(none)' rows behave the way they do.

findings.whatTheGameHas: CHECKED: Dealey's 'Two twin 76mm/50 Mk 33' carries air:1 — the Mk 33 3in/50 is the postwar dual-purpose AA mount and the mask is right. Knox's 'One 127mm/54 Mk 42' carries air:1 — right. The e00 LCS carries 'One 57mm Mk 110' — the correct gun, and it is the e20 version that has it wrong. warship_specs.js gives nato_e60_carrier guns:0.
findings.whatIsReal: Enterprise CVN-65 was commissioned with no guns at all, the first US carrier so built; Sea Sparrow BPDMS was not added until 1967. Dealey and Knox both fought aircraft with those exact mounts.
findings.fix: None. Checked and sound.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: role 'patrol' is listed in rules.js ERA_TIMELESS, which stamps from:'e50' on it, so the Mk VI is buildable in all six eras. This looks like a 65-year anachronism and is not one: rules.js lines 3600-3612 argue the case explicitly — 'between a Project 183 and a Mk VI there is a diesel' — and contrast it with capabilities that do carry a real date.
findings.whatIsReal: The Mk VI entered service in 2015. The ROLE — a fast gun-armed inshore boat — was in American hands continuously from the PT boats and PGM patrol craft of the 1950s through the PCF Swift boats of 1965 and the Cyclone-class PCs of 1993.
findings.fix: None to the mechanism. One genuine gap worth noting separately: the US is the only faction with no era-specific patrol boats at all (gbr, fra, pact, pla, kpa, roc all have them), so an American player in 1955 builds a boat labelled 'Mk VI'. Real candidates exist if the owner wants them — PGM-type gunboat, PCF Swift 1965, Asheville-class PG 1966, Cyclone-class PC 1993.

findings.whatTheGameHas: MEASURED: both carry sam_sm2 (proj missile, tgt air, r14.5) so both register as area air-defence hosts in areaSam(); vls is 96 on the Burke and 122 on the Ticonderoga; radarQ 34 and 40; sonar 9.5 and 9.0; helo 2 each; ciws 0.72 and 0.78. corvette_n has vls:8 and no SAM, so the game DOES distinguish an Aegis ship from a light escort in the present day.
findings.whatIsReal: 96 Mk 41 cells on a Flight IIA Burke and 122 on a Ticonderoga are the exact real figures. The Aegis line is drawn correctly — in one era out of six.
findings.fix: None. This is the model the other five eras should be brought up to, and edits E3-E11 do that.

edits.why: Six new American naval weapons, named OUTSIDE the w_<era>_<fac>_<role> pattern. This is forced, not stylistic: every generated naval id is carried by 2-4 nations (w_e90_nato_destroyer is on the Burke, the Type 42 Batch 3, the Cassard AND the Brandenburg), so an American correction made in the weapon table renames European ships. These six are American-only and every one is dated. sam_terrier/sam_tartar/sam_seasparrow/sam_sm2mr give the era rosters the fleet air defence they have none of; navgun_mk42 and aa_5in38 give the 1950s hulls the dual-purpose batteries that were their AA. Placed immediately before the existing European naval ordnance block, whose comment already explains the naming rule.
edits.newCode:
/* ---- American naval ordnance the era rosters were missing ----
     Named OUTSIDE the w_<era>_<fac>_<role> pattern for the same reason the
     European block below is, and for one more: every generated naval id is
     shared by two to four navies - w_e90_nato_destroyer is carried by the
     Arleigh Burke, the Type 42 Batch 3, the Cassard and the Brandenburg -
     so editing one to correct an American ship silently renames three
     European ones. These are American, dated, and carried only by American
     hulls.

     The dates are the point. Terrier went to sea on Boston in 1956 and Talos
     on Galveston in 1958; Tartar reached the fleet on Charles F. Adams in
     1962. All three are beam-riding or semi-active rounds that need a
     dedicated director illuminating the target, so a ship engages two or
     three aircraft and no more - which is the saturation problem Aegis was
     built in 1983 to solve. SM-2MR is that answer: one SPY-1 array tracks
     hundreds of contacts and the round flies most of the way on inertial
     guidance, so the illuminators are needed only in the last seconds.
     Sea Sparrow is NOT an area system and must not be read as one - it is a
     point-defence round for the ship it is bolted to, fitted from 1967
     because the carriers and the Spruances had nothing else. */

edits.why: E1 - Des Moines CA-134. The 8in main battery cannot engage aircraft and should not; what did was TWELVE 5in/38 in twin Mk 32 mounts plus a heavy 3in/50 battery. The main-battery weapon is left untouched because it is shared with HMS Swiftsure and De Grasse. Appended, never prepended: generations.js writes weapons[0] and bombard()'s fallback scan walks forward from it.

E2 - Forrest Sherman DD-931. Swapped rather than appended, because this fixes two things at once: the Mk 42 is a dual-purpose mount and the ship could shoot at aircraft, and the shared id also put 'Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts' on a British Daring, a French T 47 Surcouf and a German Fletcher. navgun_mk42's dmg/range/reload/burst/acc/speed/aoe are copied verbatim from w_e50_nato_destroyer, so nothing about the gunnery changes - only the label and the air bit.

E3 - USS Long Beach CGN-9, 1961. FATAL fix. The ship's one weapon is named 'Terrier and Talos SAM launchers' and has air:0; the desc says it was built with no guns at all. Two Mk 10 Terrier launchers forward, one Mk 12 Talos aft. The gun row is left alone because it is also carried by HMS Tiger and the Colbert.

E4 - USS Charles F. Adams DDG-2, 1960. The class the desc calls 'the first US destroyers designed from the keel up around a surface-to-air missile', with no surface-to-air missile. Mk 11 twin Tartar aft.

E5 - Oliver Hazard Perry FFG-7, 1977. Its weapon is NAMED 'Mk 13 launcher for SM-1MR and Harpoon' and is a gun. A Mk 13 arm with 40 rounds of SM-1MR and Harpoon, one Phalanx. sam_sm1 and ssm_harpoon and ciws_phalanx all already exist.

E6 - USS Spruance DD-963. Its own desc says 'the empty space then absorbed vertical launch cells and Tomahawk, making it the most heavily armed destroyer afloat by the end of the decade' and the loadout is one gun. Sea Sparrow BPDMS from commissioning (point defence, deliberately the short-ranged new round and NOT an area system), Harpoon 1981, Phalanx 1980, ASROC throughout, ABL Tomahawk from 1983 - USS Merrill fired the first Tomahawk from a surface ship that year. NOTE the measured side effect: tlam_n reaches 19 tiles and generations.js's 'eyes to match the reach' pass then raises this hull's sight from 10.9 to 19.4. That is the same thing that already happens to ssgn_n, whose sight is 19.4 for exactly this reason, so it is consistent - but it is a real vision change and the owner should see it before taking the edit.

E7 - USS Ticonderoga CG-47, commissioned 22 Jan 1983. FATAL fix, and the single most important line in this fleet. Two Mk 26 twin launchers with 68 SM-2MR, two 5in/54 Mk 45, eight Harpoon, ASROC, two Phalanx, two SH-60B. Tomahawk is deliberately NOT given here: CG-47 to CG-51 carried Mk 26 arms which could not fire it, and CG-47 is the hull this row names. sam_sm2mr rather than sam_sm2 because SM-6 is 2013.

E8 - Perry FFG-7 in the 1990s. As authored the SAME HULL loses its air-defence weapon going from e80 to e90, which is backwards: the Mk 13 came out class-wide in 2003-2004, which is the e00 period, exactly as this unit's own desc dates it.

E9 - USS Arleigh Burke DDG-51, commissioned 4 July 1991. FATAL fix. SPY-1D, 90 Mk 41 cells with SM-2MR, Tomahawk and VLA, eight Harpoon on Flight I/II, one 5in/54 Mk 45, Mk 32 tubes, two Phalanx. The weapon this hull already carries is NAMED '90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha' and is a 720 m/s shell with air:0 - the prose and the mask contradict each other on the same line. That name is NOT corrected here because w_e90_nato_destroyer is also carried by the Type 42 Batch 3, the Cassard and the Brandenburg; see the shared-weapon finding.

E10 - Ticonderoga in the 1990s, CG-52 onward, all VLS. 122 Mk 41 cells carrying SM-2MR, Tomahawk and VLA; Bunker Hill was the first Mk 41 Tomahawk ship in 1986 and fired on the opening night of Desert Storm on 17 Jan 1991. This is the only generated naval weapon in the American fleet that no other nation shares, so the array is safe to extend freely.

E11 - Arleigh Burke Flight IIA, 2000. sam_sm2 rather than sam_sm2mr because SM-6 does belong to this hull's later life. Harpoon is deliberately ABSENT, which makes the loadout agree with the unit's own desc for the first time: 'Flight IIA ... deleted the Harpoon launchers, which meant that for over a decade the standard US destroyer had no dedicated anti-ship missile at all'.

E12 - LCS-1 Freedom and LCS-2 Independence, 2008. Freedom carries a 21-cell Mk 49 RAM launcher, Independence an 11-cell SeaRAM. Not a Phalanx gun, and not an area system - sam_ram reaches 4.6 tiles, which is local cover and nothing more. sam_ram already exists and is already used by the German K130 and F124.

E13 - nato_e90_corvette radar cross-section. 0.1 made a 1977 boxy single-screw Perry the stealthiest surface ship in the game bar one, stealthier than a Tuo Chiang or a Type 45, while the IDENTICAL e80 Perry hull sits at 0.6. It is a copy of corvette_n's value on the wrong row. SHIP_RCS drives detection range and missile lock, so it is not cosmetic. This anchor is the tail of the nato_e90_corvette line and is unique in the file.

E14 - the e20 LCS. Three places in this codebase already say 57mm - the unit's own desc, warship_specs.js gunCal:57, and the e00 version of the same ship carrying 'One 57mm Mk 110' - and the loadout said 76mm Italian. This is the exact case generations.js's own NAVGUN comment complains about ('every navy was firing the same Italian gun'), left unfixed for the Americans because NAVGUN has no nato row. Both replacement ids already exist.

proof:
WHAT WAS MEASURED (jsc, on a concatenation of a `var window=this;` stub + js/util.js + js/config.js + js/facts.js + js/rules.js + js/eras.js + js/heavyair.js + js/generations.js, so every figure is post-generations.js):

BASELINE, on the live repo:
- 1132 units, 1686 weapons, 232 cat:"naval" defs, 176 layer:"sea".
- 26 US surface hulls enumerated with resolved weapon ids, names, tgt masks, proj, range, dmg, acc (full listing in `inventory`).
- Area air defence, tested against the actual rule in combat.js areaSam() (`tgt.air && proj === "missile"`): 2 of 26 US surface hulls pass, both e20-roster. 0 of 20 era-roster hulls. Across all eight factions, the only era-roster ships that pass are pact_e60/e90/e00_carrier, and they pass because the Moskva's "14 x Ka-25 ASW helicopters" was authored as proj:"missile", tgt:{air:1}.
- Tomahawk: `tlam_n` is carried by exactly one American unit in the game, ssgn_n. Zero surface hulls.

TOMAHAWK INFLATES SIGHT. generations.js's 'eyes to match the reach' pass raises a unit's sight to its longest non-arc weapon range + 0.4. tlam_n reaches 19, so every hull given it goes to sight 19.4: the Spruance from 10.9, the e90 Burke from 11.4, the e90 Ticonderoga from 11.0, the e00 Burke from 11.8, and cruiser_n/destroyer_n from 14.9. This is exactly what already happens to ssgn_n (sight 19.4 for the same reason), so it is consistent with the existing model - but a Burke that sees 19.4 tiles is a large sensor change and may move the AI's behaviour. If that is unwanted, the fix that matches the release-authority commit already in the tree is to mark tlam_n `manual`, which is a separate design decision I did not make.
